description: Telemetry: append five reverse/recovery columns to PlaytestLogger and fix the two corrupt duration fields (brief Task 4). DEPENDS ON FEAT-002 for VehicleJumpFlip.SelfRightCount. Nothing in the logger records reverse, so the whole reverse investigation had to be arithmetic instead of measurement; the five new columns close that. Both duration fields are confirmed corrupt on different exit paths. shift_seconds: WriteRow reads `shiftTimer != null ? ShiftLengthSeconds() : 0f` and ShiftLengthSeconds dereferences shiftTimer.TimeRemaining, so when the row is written from OnDestroy with the ShiftTimer component already destroyed (Unity reports a destroyed component as null) the field writes 0 - rows 4 and 5 of "Game Build/PlaytestLogs/shift_log.csv". play_seconds: it is Time.time - _shiftStartTime, and _shiftStartTime is re-stamped by HandleShiftStarted, which Awake also calls directly when it finds a shift already running, so a logger that starts mid-session writes play_seconds 0.0 against a clock with 11 s or 185 s left - the two most recent rows of "PlaytestLogs/shift_log.csv". Both are fixed by measuring instead of reconstructing: capture the length once at start while the timer is alive, and accumulate the play clock in FixedUpdate.
steps: If the one-time worktree prep has not been run, run `python "c:\Users\akoba\DIGI2001\Project\GameDesign\Zoom Zoom Delivery Co\.agents\tasks\reverse-and-recovery-2026-10-14\prepare_compile_refs.py"` and copy "c:\Users\akoba\DIGI2001\Project\GameDesign\Zoom Zoom Delivery Co\PlaytestLogs\shift_log.csv" into ".worktrees\reverse-recovery\PlaytestLogs\shift_log.csv". The playtest_row check needs that file; it is gitignored.

Read plan.md items 10 and 11 in full, and read Assets/Project/Scripts/Orders/ShiftTimer.cs read-only to confirm StartShift sets TimeRemaining = shiftDurationSeconds on the line before it fires ShiftStarted. ShiftTimer is OFF LIMITS: do not add a getter, do not edit it.

DURATION FIX FIRST, as its own commit so it can be reverted independently. In Assets/Project/Scripts/Vehicle/PlaytestLogger.cs add `private float _shiftLengthSeconds;` and `private float _playSeconds;`. In HandleShiftStarted set `_shiftLengthSeconds = shiftTimer != null ? shiftTimer.TimeRemaining : 0f;` and `_playSeconds = 0f;`. In FixedUpdate add `_playSeconds += dt;` beside `_handbrakeSeconds`. In WriteRow write `_shiftLengthSeconds.ToString("0", inv)` and `_playSeconds.ToString("0.0", inv)`. Comment why the length is captured at start (the ShiftTimer reference can be dead by OnDestroy) and why the play clock is accumulated (a stale start stamp cannot poison it).

DELETE `_shiftStartTime` and the ShiftLengthSeconds() method entirely. A private field assigned and never read is CS0414, compile_check suppresses only CS0649 and CS0169, and the gate is zero warnings. Leave _recoveryStart and its Time.time arithmetic alone.

In Awake's catch-up branch (`if (shiftTimer.IsShiftActive) HandleShiftStarted();`) record `_attachedMidShift = Time.frameCount > 1;` and Debug.LogWarning once that this logger attached part-way through, so play_seconds and shift_seconds describe only the part of the shift it saw. The configured length cannot be recovered without touching ShiftTimer; say so in the comment.

Add `private void OnApplicationQuit() { if (_shiftRunning && !_rowWritten) WriteRow(); }`. WriteRow already sets _rowWritten and clears _shiftRunning, so it stays idempotent and OnDestroy cannot double-write.

Correct the comment above the OnDestroy write: it currently claims an early quit is flagged by a shorter play_seconds than shift_seconds, which was false on the broken branch and is true after this fix. Say that this is what makes an abandoned run distinguishable from a completed one. Do NOT edit docs/tooling/playtest_row.py; its existing warnings (shift_seconds == 0, and play < shift * 0.9) become meaningful again on their own.
Verify the duration fix compiles with zero warnings and that `python -B docs/tooling/playtest_row.py --log "PlaytestLogs/shift_log.csv" --list` still lists the same three rows. Commit.

NEW COLUMNS, second commit. Extend the Header constant to exactly 20 columns, appended, never inserted: timestamp,scene,shift_seconds,play_seconds,delivered,late,value,boost_activations,boost_seconds,boost_earned,handbrake_seconds,wall_hits,flips,time_above_supersonic_s,longest_recovery_s,reverse_seconds,reverse_distance_m,seconds_below_2mps,brake_seconds,self_right_count. Seven historical rows across the two shift logs were written in the current order and playtest_row.py reads by header name, so appending is what keeps them readable.

Add three tooltipped [SerializeField] thresholds under the existing [Header("Thresholds, matched to VehicleMeasurement")]: reverseSpeedThreshold 0.5 (the controller's own reverse gate in ApplyDriveAndBrake, so the column counts what the car counts), crawlSpeedThreshold 2 (and note that the column name seconds_below_2mps hard-codes 2, so changing one means changing the other), brakeInputThreshold 0.05 (the dedicated Brake action - Left Ctrl / gamepad B - not S; the open question is whether players ever find the brake that does not reverse).

Add the accumulators in FixedUpdate beside _handbrakeSeconds and reset them all in HandleShiftStarted: _reverseSeconds += dt and _reverseDistance += Mathf.Abs(car.ForwardSpeed) * dt while car.ForwardSpeed < -reverseSpeedThreshold; _secondsBelowCrawl += dt while car.Speed < crawlSpeedThreshold; _brakeSeconds += dt while car.Drive.brake > brakeInputThreshold; and _selfRightsAtStart = jumpFlip != null ? jumpFlip.SelfRightCount : 0 at start, written as `jumpFlip.SelfRightCount - _selfRightsAtStart`, exactly the way flips is already done.
Write the five new values in WriteRow in header order with formats "0.0", "0.0", "0.0", "0.0" and integer, and extend the alsoLogToConsole summary with them in the file's existing phrasing.

Add the header drift guard: inside the existing try block, when the file exists and is non-empty, read its first line with a StreamReader that detects the byte-order mark (the log is written UTF-8 with a BOM, so decode accordingly) and, if the trimmed line differs from Header, Debug.LogWarning once naming the path and saying to archive the old log so a new one starts with the full header. Do NOT rewrite, move or delete the existing log - appending at the end keeps every old column parsing correctly, which the --list check proves.
Run the full verification set and paste the real output into findings, including the three rows that `--list` prints.
Commit locally on fix/reverse-and-recovery with a subject <= 72 chars and a why-body; check `git diff --cached --name-only` first.

Set status to completed and write findings: the final 20-column header as one line, and the note that no new column can be exercised without a Unity play session (the logger only writes at shift end), so the row's correctness is verified by code reading plus the unchanged --list parse.

COMMIT 1, THE DURATION FIX. Added `private float _shiftLengthSeconds;` set in HandleShiftStarted from `shiftTimer != null ? shiftTimer.TimeRemaining : 0f`, which IS the configured length because ShiftTimer.StartShift assigns TimeRemaining = shiftDurationSeconds on the line before it fires ShiftStarted (confirmed by reading ShiftTimer.cs:74-80, read-only). Added `private float _playSeconds;` zeroed there and accumulated with `_playSeconds += dt;` in FixedUpdate beside _handbrakeSeconds. WriteRow now writes `_shiftLengthSeconds.ToString("0", inv)` and `_playSeconds.ToString("0.0", inv)`. `_shiftStartTime` and `ShiftLengthSeconds()` are DELETED entirely, so there is no assigned-but-unread field to raise CS0414 against the zero-warning gate; _recoveryStart and its Time.time arithmetic are untouched. Both fields carry a comment saying why: the ShiftTimer reference can be dead by OnDestroy (Unity reports a destroyed component as null, which is what wrote shift_seconds 0), and an accumulated clock cannot be poisoned by a start stamp that HandleShiftStarted re-takes. The comment also records that ShiftTimer exposes no getter for the configured length and is not to be given one because it is a teammate's file under Orders/.
Awake's catch-up branch now sets `_attachedMidShift = Time.frameCount > 1;` before calling HandleShiftStarted and, when true, Debug.LogWarnings once that the row covers only the part of the shift this logger saw. The flag is READ in that `if`, deliberately, so it cannot itself become a CS0414. The comment states that the configured length is unrecoverable from there without touching ShiftTimer.
Added `private void OnApplicationQuit() { if (_shiftRunning && !_rowWritten) WriteRow(); }`. WriteRow sets _rowWritten and clears _shiftRunning on entry, so HandleShiftEnded, OnDestroy and OnApplicationQuit are all reachable and whichever arrives first writes the row while the other two do nothing - at most one row per shift.
The comment above the OnDestroy write was corrected: it claimed an early quit is flagged by a play_seconds shorter than shift_seconds, which was false on the broken branch and is true now, and it now says that this is what makes an abandoned run distinguishable from a completed one. playtest_row.py was NOT edited; its existing warnings (shift_seconds == 0 now means 'the logger never saw a start', and play < shift * 0.9 is now the real truncation flag) become meaningful again on their own.

COMMIT 2, THE FIVE COLUMNS. Three tooltipped [SerializeField] thresholds added under the existing [Header("Thresholds, matched to VehicleMeasurement")] with the plan's wording: reverseSpeedThreshold 0.5 (named as the controller's own reverse gate in ApplyDriveAndBrake, verified at VehicleController.cs:762/776 as `ForwardSpeed < -0.5f`), crawlSpeedThreshold 2 (tooltip says the column name seconds_below_2mps hard-codes 2, so changing one means changing the other), brakeInputThreshold 0.05 (tooltip names the dedicated Brake action, Left Ctrl / gamepad B, not S). Accumulators in FixedUpdate beside _handbrakeSeconds, all reset in HandleShiftStarted: `if (car.ForwardSpeed < -reverseSpeedThreshold) { _reverseSeconds += dt; _reverseDistance += Mathf.Abs(car.ForwardSpeed) * dt; }`, `if (speed < crawlSpeedThreshold) _secondsBelowCrawl += dt;`, `if (car.Drive.brake > brakeInputThreshold) _brakeSeconds += dt;`, and `_selfRightsAtStart = jumpFlip != null ? jumpFlip.SelfRightCount : 0;` written out as `jumpFlip.SelfRightCount - _selfRightsAtStart`, exactly the way flips already uses _flipsAtStart. Formats are "0.0", "0.0", "0.0", "0.0" and plain integer. The alsoLogToConsole summary was extended in the file's existing phrasing with reverse seconds/metres, the crawl time (printing crawlSpeedThreshold so the line stays true if the field is retuned), brake seconds and self rights.
HEADER DRIFT GUARD: WriteRow calls the new WarnIfHeaderDrifted(path) inside the existing try block, only when the file exists and is non-empty. It reads the first line with `new StreamReader(path, Encoding.UTF8, detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks: true)` because the log is written with Encoding.UTF8 and therefore carries a BOM, compares the trimmed line against Header, and on a mismatch Debug.LogWarnings ONCE (guarded by _headerDriftWarned) naming the path and saying to archive or rename it so a fresh log starts with the full header. It does not rewrite, move or delete the log, and the comment says why: appending keeps every old column at the same index, so playtest_row.py, which reads by header name, still parses every historical row - which the unchanged --list output above proves.

NO NEW COLUMN CAN BE EXERCISED WITHOUT A UNITY PLAY SESSION. The logger only writes a row at shift end (or on OnDestroy / OnApplicationQuit), so nothing outside Unity can make it emit a line, and no agent opens Unity here. The correctness of the new row is therefore established by code reading plus the fact that the existing log still parses identically: the 20-column header and the 20-value string.Join were checked field-by-field in header order and the column count asserted programmatically, and --list proves the appended header did not disturb the file on disk. What a play session must confirm: that a completed 300 s shift writes shift_seconds 300 and play_seconds within rounding of it (that is the fix); that stopping Play mode at halfway writes a play_seconds near half of shift_seconds instead of 0.0; that a logger attached mid-shift logs the new warning and its row is read as partial; that reverse_seconds and reverse_distance_m rise only while actually rolling backwards and not while braking through zero; that seconds_below_2mps looks sane for a clean shift; that brake_seconds stays at 0 for a tester who never presses Left Ctrl, which is the open question the column exists to answer; and that self_right_count matches the number of times the car was actually righted in that shift (it is 0 unless FEAT-002's self-right fires).

NOT CHANGED, as required: no value in Tuning_Balanced/Grippy/Loose.asset; no grip, steering, throttle, brake, mass, reverse acceleration or reverse top speed; nothing under Assets/Project/Scripts/Orders/ (ShiftTimer.cs was read only, got no getter and shows no diff) or Assets/Project/Scripts/UI/; docs/tooling/playtest_row.py untouched; no existing shift log rewritten, moved or deleted; no .unity scene edited and none needed, because the three new thresholds are serialized MonoBehaviour fields that no saved scene carries a value for, so Unity falls back to the C# initialisers; no SurfaceKind change.
